title: Redwood Console — Tracing + Request Logs Debugging Demo
summary: AE + SE demo of Redwood Console focusing on tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer cares about debugging production failures, multi-tenant observability, and data residency. Agreed next step: Redwood to run a short in-house benchmark and share security/compliance docs; schedule pilot kickoff script for next week.
next_steps: Share short benchmark plan + telemetry requirements (Carlos)
Provide pricing sketch for dedicated capacity (Maya)
action_items: Maya Chen: send SOC2/ISO + compliance packet by 2027-03-12
Carlos Ruiz: draft benchmark plan and required telemetry specs by 2027-03-13
Priya Sharma: confirm pilot participants and SSO details by 2027-03-12
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-03-10
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Recording: Zoom (auto)
- Attendees: Maya Chen, Carlos Ruiz (Redwood); Priya Sharma, Ben Carter, Lina Gomez (Atlas)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, we'll walk through the console tracing and request logs stuff, feel free to interrupt.
[00:10] Priya Sharma: thanks maya, big thing for us is being able to debug failures when our summarization pipeline drops hallucinations — we need to track per-request model version, token counts, and kv cache hits if possible.
[00:25] Carlos Ruiz: yeah totally, that's what we'll focus on: tracing ties together the request id to model variant, kernel path, and any fallbacks. we'll show how error analysis surfaces patterns.
[00:40] Ben Carter: quick infra note, we're on GCP in us-central1, considering dedicated GPUs later. also strict data residency, need private deployment options.
[00:50] Lina Gomez: also SOC2 and SSO are must-haves.
[01:05] Maya Chen: noted, we'll point out audit logs and the compliance pack at the end. ok carlos, demo.
[01:12] Carlos Ruiz: opening the console — bear with me, slow spin — ok main nav: tracing, request logs, error analysis. first tab is traces: you can search by request id, model name, or route. i'll search for a recent failing trace.
[01:35] Speaker 2: (inaudible) it shows the timeline with kernel switches, batching groups, and a KV cache hit counter — sometimes the transcriber writes kv as k v, you get the idea.
[01:50] Carlos Ruiz: right, and here we show per-span metadata: start/end, latency, backend node id, quantization profile used. if you click a span you can see the effective kernel selection — e.g., flash-attn vs default.
[02:10] Priya Sharma: can that show when we fell back from fp16 to fp32 or to a smaller model? we need to correlate regression with fallback events.
[02:22] Carlos Ruiz: yes, fallback events are flagged. here's an example where the scheduler routed to a lower tier due to capacity and you can see the fallback reason and matched policy.
[02:35] Ben Carter: how are logs retained? we need 12 months for audits.
[02:42] Maya Chen: retention is configurable per-customer; for Dedicated/Private we can plug into your cloud storage or ship logs to your SIEM. retention UI is in settings.
[02:55] Lina Gomez: and encryption at rest — KMS?
[03:00] Carlos Ruiz: yep, KMS/HSM integrations; we'll share the concrete docs.
[03:12] Maya Chen: jumping to error analysis — show that.
[03:15] Carlos Ruiz: error analysis aggregates failed requests by error class, user-visible error codes, and model outputs. here's a cluster of prompt-timeouts and another cluster of truncated outputs. clicking into a cluster surfaces sample requests and a diff view against the golden prompt set.
[03:40] Priya Sharma: the diff view is great — can we attach our eval sets and have automated regression alerts?
[03:47] Carlos Ruiz: absolutely, Redwood Optimize ties into that to watch quality metrics and send regression alerts. we can also attach thresholds so you only get paged when a degradation crosses X%.
[04:02] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[04:10] Carlos Ruiz: now request logs — you can filter by time range, route, model, and tag like customer_id. here's a filter for requests that used model-bert-slim and had >100ms backend latency.
[04:28] Ben Carter: can filters be saved/shared with teammates?
[04:32] Carlos Ruiz: yes saved queries, and you can create dashboards that show latency percentiles and failure rates per-route.
[04:40] Priya Sharma: about PII — do request logs redact user-provided text by default? we can't store raw PII in logs.
[04:50] Carlos Ruiz: default hosted logs keep only metadata; payload retention is configurable. for Private deployments we can enable payload redaction or route payloads to your flakeless S3 with server-side encryption.
[05:05] Lina Gomez: show me a live debug flow for a request that resulted in a bad output.
[05:12] Carlos Ruiz: ok i have a recent request id — pulling it up. [05:20] shows the request timeline: tokenization, kv cache hit 0, model forward 1.2s, decoder 0.9s. output tokens show a sudden truncation at 128 tokens with an error code 503.
[05:40] Priya Sharma: 503 from where? upstream?
[05:44] Carlos Ruiz: this is the runtime returning TRUNC_OUTPUT error when it hits the per-request token cap — here you can see the enforced max tokens from the route config (defaults) and a canary that applied a lower cap.
[05:58] Ben Carter: can we set per-customer overrides so power users get higher caps?
[06:04] Carlos Ruiz: yes route-level overrides and tiered configs. we'll show policy rollouts later.
[06:12] Maya Chen: also note the trace links to the autoscaler logs — you can see a spike in queue depth right before the event. that often correlates with batching latency.
[06:25] Priya Sharma: how granular is the tracing — can it show kernel-level perf counters?
[06:30] Carlos Ruiz: we surface a subset — e.g., FLOPS estimates, memory pressure, batch sizes, and approx kernel time. for privacy and noise reasons we don't dump device-level traces to hosted logs unless customer opts in.
[06:50] Lina Gomez: what about cross-region fallbacks? if primary region is down, will traces show the fallback chain?
[06:58] Carlos Ruiz: yes, the routing span shows region and capacity tier decisions, and fallback spans are clearly labeled with reason codes.
[07:10] Maya Chen: quick question for atlas — what's your expected qps and p50 latency target?
[07:18] Priya Sharma: for summaries about 300 qps peak, p50 < 120ms ideally. p95 can be higher but we want p99 < 800ms.
[07:30] Carlos Ruiz: noted — that aligns with our dedicated tier guidance. we'll include a capacity sketch in the benchmark plan.
[07:42] Pria Sharma: (typo)
[07:45] Ben Carter: for the pilot, we want to run synthetic traffic and then a small percentage of real traffic, plus a canary to validate model parity.
[07:55] Carlos Ruiz: perfect — the console supports canary rollouts, and traces are automatically tagged by rollout ID. you can compare metrics side-by-side.
[08:10] Priya Sharma: can alerts be integrated with our pagerduty?
[08:14] Maya Chen: yes, integrations include PagerDuty, OpsGenie, and Slack. alerting rules can be per-route.
[08:22] Carlos Ruiz: returning to the UI — the request detail view also provides a raw json export of the trace and logs (with redaction options). here's an example where the tokenization step included odd unicode that increased token counts leading to unexpected cost.
[08:44] Lina Gomez: about cost — do we get per-token breakdowns by model and kernel?
[08:50] Carlos Ruiz: yes the console shows token-level cost and a breakdown by inference stage and model variant. we also surface suggestions from Redwood Optimize like quantization profile and batching settings.
[09:05] Priya Sharma: are there limits to how long we can keep request logs for the hosted offering?
[09:10] Maya Chen: for hosted we have default retention tiers (30/90/365) based on plan; Dedicated/Private gives you full control and S3-style retention.
[09:22] Ben Carter: curious about on-prem — do we still get the same console experience?
[09:26] Carlos Ruiz: with Private we provide a control plane that can be customer-managed; the console UI is the same, but logs and data stay within your VPC. ops integrations are local.
[09:38] Speaker 3: (crosstalk)
[09:45] Carlos Ruiz: open the error analysis 'root cause' tool — it aggregates traces by root cause heuristics: quota, fallback, kernel OOM, and model regression. clicking kernel OOM shows stack of spans and memory usage.
[10:05] Priya Sharma: do you surface the model's batch size history? sometimes a burst increases batch and causes increased tail latency.
[10:12] Carlos Ruiz: yes we show batch size distribution over time and correlated p99. you can drill into the exact batch composition if you opt in to that telemetry.
[10:25] Lina Gomez: security question — where are audit logs for config changes stored? we need immutable logs for compliance.
[10:33] Maya Chen: audit logs are write-once to your configured audit storage; for hosted we can integrate with your SIEM and provide signed logs.
[10:42] Priya Sharma: great. can you demo a troubleshooting scenario end-to-end?
[10:46] Carlos Ruiz: sure — scenario A: customer sees increase in hallucinations after a model swap. step 1, filter traces by rollout-id; step 2, run error analysis to compare output quality vs golden set; step 3, inspect request logs for tokenization and kv-cache hit rates; step 4, if fallback was used, check routing spans. here's a saved workflow that does exactly that.
[11:18] Ben Carter: that workflow/export is useful — can it be automated for on-call?
[11:22] Carlos Ruiz: yes you can tie it to an alert trigger so when drift exceeds threshold the workflow runs and posts a summary to Slack with top traces.
[11:32] Priya Sharma: in the saved workflow can we attach notes and ownership? we want the SRE to see context.
[11:38] Carlos Ruiz: saved runs include annotations and a permalink to the trace.
[11:45] Maya Chen: jumping away from UI, a couple of how-we'd-run items: for the pilot we'll want sample telemetry, a small corpus of golden prompts, and an SSO test user.
[11:58] Priya Sharma: we'll provide that. timeline — we want pilot in two weeks.
[12:04] Maya Chen: good, we'll aim to get security docs and a benchmark plan out in two business days.
[12:12] Carlos Ruiz: last thing — request logs can be exported real-time via stream to your Kafka/SQS or batched to cloud storage. any preference?
[12:24] Ben Carter: Kafka for real-time alerting is preferred.
[12:28] Carlos Ruiz: noted.
[12:32] Lina Gomez: are there any gotchas with GDPR when streaming logs cross-region?
[12:38] Maya Chen: data residency controls allow region pinning; streaming across regions is off by default — we'll ensure configs respect GDPR.
[12:46] Priya Sharma: can we see an example of the JSON trace export?
[12:50] Carlos Ruiz: pasting snippet — shows top-level spans, timestamps, model_version, route_config, rollout_id, device_metrics; note some of the field names are slightly different in the transcript because of auto-transcribe.
[13:10] Speaker 1: (laughter)
[13:15] Carlos Ruiz: wrapping up, recap: we'll send SOC2 + ISO docs, benchmark plan, and sketch pricing for a dedicated pilot. next meeting to confirm pilot kickoff next week.
[13:30] Priya Sharma: thanks all, this was helpful. one last ask — can you include sample alert rules for hallucination detection?
[13:40] Maya Chen: yes we'll include recommended rules and a sample PagerDuty config.
[13:45] Lina Gomez: thanks.
[13:50] Carlos Ruiz: any final q's?
[13:53] Ben Carter: none here.
[14:00] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

Footer notes:
- Transcript has occasional misattributions and minor transcription errors.
- Several links were referenced during the demo: \"Pilot plan (link)\", \"Compliance packet (link)\", \"Benchmark spreadsheet (link)\" — these will be attached to the CRM note.
